about.title: Personal Injury Help in Burlingame, California
about.longDescription: Burlingame's streets carry a steady mix of local traffic and commuters cutting through on US-101, California Drive, and El Camino Real (SR-82/Rt 82). Public records for the most recent full year show 104 injury collisions in the city, with 140 people hurt and 3 lives lost — numbers that reflect how much everyday driving, walking, and biking happens along these corridors. Whether you were hurt near one of these roads, in a parking lot, or somewhere else in town, the days after an injury are often confusing: medical visits, insurance calls, missed work. LawProactive is a free service that helps injured people in Burlingame connect with an independent personal injury attorney who can look at what happened and explain your options. We are not a law firm, we don't decide claims, and we don't charge anything for the connection. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there is a recovery. Reaching out costs you nothing and doesn't commit you to anything — it just gets you talking to someone who handles these cases regularly.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You have time, but not forever
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to act sooner rather than later.

items.title: Shared fault doesn't shut the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still pursue compensation — it's just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No ceiling on pain and suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life.

items.title: You don't pay unless there's a recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so legal fees only come out of money recovered on your behalf — nothing upfront.

items.question: How much does it cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney. We are not a law firm and don't charge fees for making the connection.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the injury under California's statute of limitations. If your claim involves a government agency, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation promptly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Burlingame?
items.answer: Public crash records point to higher collision counts along corridors like US-101, California Drive, and El Camino Real (SR-82/Rt 82), with reported crashes tending to peak on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. These are neutral collision counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Do I have to pay upfront for an attorney?
items.answer: No. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no fee unless there's a recovery.
